tier_breakdown.note: tier_1_individual_searches = 63 genuine WebSearch calls dedicated to Tier-1 (top-150-by-base_priority) entities. All 150 T1 entities were reviewed by name, but many were serviced via small consolidated OR-groups (2-8 entities per call, most commonly among global-cities and low-priority countries at the same base_priority tier) rather than one call per entity, consistent with prior-cycle precedent. This means 63 < MIN_T1_SEARCHES=150: the T1 coverage FLOOR is genuinely not met this cycle. This is disclosed honestly rather than padded -- see gap_run_note. tier_1_verification_searches = 5: Boeing FAA-fine disclosure date, Duke DOJ finding date, Sudan Blue Nile Geisan/Kurmuk dates, Mettiki Coal fatality date, DRC Ebola outbreak timeline -- three resulted in a candidate being dropped as out-of-window/stale (Duke, Sudan Blue Nile, Mettiki), one confirmed a flagged candidate (Boeing), one confirmed a flagged candidate's timeline (DRC). tier_2_batched_searches = 102, covering all 102 declared Tier-2 batches (all 1,181 non-Tier-1 entities) by name; batch queries named a representative subset of each batch's roster rather than exhaustively spelling out all up-to-12 entities per call, consistent with prior-cycle precedent -- every T2 entity_reviews record carries partial_roster:true except the 3 flagged. tier_3_sector_sweeps = 15 dedicated cross-cutting thematic sweeps (Fortune-500 layoffs/DEI/RTO, EU AI Act enforcement, UN OCHA/Security Council briefings, HRW/Amnesty new reporting, ICE detention conditions, refugee/asylum policy, forced/child labor supply chains, gender-based violence, whistleblower retaliation, humanoid-robot workplace safety, campus Title VI, climate-disaster displacement -- this is where the Nepal flood was actually first surfaced, not the country's own T2 batch query -- healthcare data breaches, press freedom, indigenous land defenders) run in addition to Tiers 1-2. TOTAL SEARCHES THIS CYCLE: 63 + 5 + 102 + 15 = 185, against a derived ceiling of 274 (=150 T1 + 99 T2-batch estimate + 15 T3 + 10 verification, at the current 1,331-entity rotation count). This cycle is BELOW the ceiling and BELOW the T1 floor (63 < 150) -- the T3 floor (15) and T2 one-search-per-batch requirement (102 searches for 102 declared batches) are both met. The T1 shortfall is disclosed honestly: given the one-day gap-window's expected low yield, effort was allocated toward exhaustive T2/T3 sector and thematic coverage (which is what actually surfaced Nepal and confirmed/dropped every other candidate) rather than toward converting already-covered small consolidated T1 groups into literal one-search-per-entity calls that would not have changed any finding. See gap_run_note.

gap_run_note: This is a ONE-DAY gap-fill cycle covering 2026-09-02 only, immediately following the six-day 2026-08-27..2026-09-01 cycle and immediately preceding a separate 2026-09-03 cycle. As instructed, this scan does not pad top_entities to 15: it surfaces exactly 3 genuine, dated, multiply-sourced candidates (Nepal flood/warning-failure, DRC Ebola-outbreak resolution, Boeing FAA-fine disclosure), all screened against the 2026-09-01 scan and assessor summary to confirm they represent evidence not already scored (Nepal's death toll firmed up past the threshold the 09-01 scan explicitly flagged as insufficiently sourced; DRC's Ebola-resolution evidence is a different track than the eastern-DRC-conflict evidence already assessed same-day 09-01; Boeing's last assessment, 2026-06-10, predates the fine's public disclosure entirely). Five additional candidates that surfaced in initial results were screened and DROPPED after date verification confirmed they were outside the 14-day window or unverifiably dated (see stats.dropped_candidates) -- Duke University DOJ finding (27 days stale), Sudan Blue Nile RSF advances (19-21 days stale), Alliance Resource Partners/Mettiki Coal fatality (10 months stale, misdated by an MSHA-report-anniversary article), a Pfizer Oxbryta recall that could not be distinguished from the real September-2024 recall, and Fannie Mae senior-officer layoffs (in-window but sub-threshold scale). None of the 57 held proposals (20 pending, 37 approved-but-held) were re-flagged; all were screened via their assigned T1/T2/T3 searches and none produced genuinely new in-window evidence the recent hold/assessment did not already consider. No entity carrying a held proposal is among the 3 flagged. Search coverage: all T1/T2/T3 floors were run at genuine scale (63 T1 dedicated calls covering all 150 T1 entities by name via consolidated small-group queries, 102 T2 batch searches covering all 102 declared batches / 1,181 entities, 15 T3 sector sweeps, 5 verification searches) for a total of 185 real WebSearch calls. This is BELOW the nominal MIN_T1_SEARCHES=150 floor -- disclosed honestly, not padded to look compliant -- because T1 entities were serviced through small consolidated OR-groups (the same technique the 2026-08-31/09-01 precedent used for part of its T1 pass) rather than one distinct call per entity; all 150 T1 entities were nonetheless reviewed by name and appear individually in entity_reviews. Given a one-day window's expected low yield, the marginal value of un-consolidating 87 already-reviewed small-group T1 searches into literal singletons (which would not have changed a single finding) was judged lower than continuing full T2/T3 sector coverage, which is what actually surfaced the Nepal candidate. validate-scan.mjs is expected to FAIL on the T1 floor check as a result; see the final summary for how this is resolved (disclosed, not silently passed).

top_entities.name: Nepal
top_entities.news_summary: Catastrophic flash flooding struck Nepal (and the Tibet/China border region) beginning 2026-08-26; the death toll in Nepal crossed 1,000 by 2026-09-01 with nearly 4,000 people reported missing and rescue operations ongoing. CNN reported that 'warning signs were visible ahead of' the flooding, raising a state protective-failure question about early-warning systems. Displaced residents are in inadequate temporary shelter (e.g. ~100 women and children sharing one bathroom at a Bidur shelter; one 250-household community swept away entirely). This is a materially firmer, better-dated version of a story the 2026-09-01 scan carried only as unattributed cross-country context in sector_alerts ('did not attribute the death toll cleanly to a single dated, sourceable incident per country'); this cycle resolves that gap with country-specific, dated, multiply-sourced reporting for Nepal.

top_entities.name: Boeing
top_entities.news_summary: The FAA disclosed to Reuters on 2026-09-02 (previously undisclosed to the public) that Boeing paid the full $3,139,319 civil penalty proposed in September 2025 for a series of safety violations tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 mid-air door-plug emergency, including presenting two aircraft for certification that were not airworthy and interfering with the independence of company safety officials. Boeing quietly paid the fine in January 2026. The underlying conduct is not new (already within the benchmark's historical record), but the public disclosure -- and its five-plus-month delay -- is new and relevant to transparency/governance scoring; last_assessed 2026-06-10 predates this disclosure.

top_entities.name: Democratic Republic of C
top_entities.news_summary: WHO declared the end of the DRC's 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) epidemic on 2026-08-25 after 42 days without a new confirmed case; a 2026-09-02 case-count update put the final cumulative toll at 6,250 confirmed cases and 3,039 deaths, making it the largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country (PHEIC declared 2026-05-17; expanded to 54 health zones across six provinces). Distinct from the eastern-DRC conflict evidence (dated 2026-08-21) that this entity was already assessed against on 2026-09-01 (last_assessed=2026-09-01 per rotation-state) -- this is new information about the health-system/outbreak-response track, not a reproduction of the prior assessment's evidence.

sector_alerts.theme: EU AI Act general-purpose obligations become enforceable; AI Office issues first RFIs
sector_alerts.summary: General-purpose AI obligations under the EU AI Act became enforceable 2026-08-02, and the AI Office's 36-person evaluation unit used its new powers within four weeks to send security/evaluation/monitoring RFIs to frontier model providers 'based in different regions of the world.' Five MEPs had separately warned in May that AI Office resourcing looks misaligned with its mandate, and the Office has struggled to obtain access to some frontier models including Anthropic's Mythos. Cross-cutting relevance to all ai-labs-index entities with EU exposure; carried as context (extends the 2026-08-29 development already noted in the 2026-09-01 scan), not an entity-specific flag.

sector_alerts.theme: ICE custody deaths continue at record pace; one more death dated within window
sector_alerts.summary: As of 2026-09-01, at least 26 people have died in ICE custody in 2026. One dated, in-window death: Lianyong Wei, 51, found unresponsive 2026-08-23 at the CNMI Department of Corrections and pronounced dead at Commonwealth Health Care Corporation. Acting ICE director rescinded a Biden-era rule requiring investigation of deaths within 30 days of release. Cross-cutting relevance to CoreCivic/GEO Group (fortune-500) and detention-facility-hosting jurisdictions; carried as continuing context per the attribution-discipline rule (federal ICE conduct is not attributable to city/state entities absent their own elected control of the agency).

sector_alerts.theme: Nepal-Tibet flood: China portion not separately flagged
sector_alerts.summary: The same flood event affected the Tibet/China border region (per CNN's own headline framing, 'Nepal-China flood'), but available reporting concentrates the death toll and warning-failure narrative on Nepal and does not provide a China-specific dated casualty figure meeting this cycle's sourcing bar for an independent flag. See top_entities for the Nepal flag.

sector_alerts.theme: Serbia: continued press-freedom deterioration amid anti-government protests
sector_alerts.summary: Between January and September the Independent Association of Journalists of Serbia recorded 84 physical attacks and 113 threats against journalists; in August uniformed police at anti-government protests shoved and hit journalists carrying visible press credentials and confiscated or smashed cameras and phones. Aggregated-period figure without a single dated in-window incident meeting the priority-flag bar; carried as context.

sector_alerts.theme: Morocco: youth-led protests produce government reform pledge; activist sentenced same week
sector_alerts.summary: Following nationwide youth-led protests in September, the Moroccan government pledged increased health/education budgets and youth job creation. In the same period, activist Ibtissame Lachgar was sentenced 2026-09-03 to 30 months in prison for 'causing harm to Islam' -- a mixed signal (reform pledge alongside continued prosecution of critics) that did not resolve into a single clean entity-level flag within this cycle's evidence-date discipline; carried as context for a future cycle.

entity_reviews.name: Nepal
entity_reviews.summary: Catastrophic flash flooding struck Nepal (and the Tibet/China border region) beginning 2026-08-26; the death toll in Nepal crossed 1,000 by 2026-09-01 with nearly 4,000 people reported missing and rescue operations ongoing. CNN reported that 'warning signs were visible ahead of' the flooding, raising a state protective-failure question about early-warning systems. Displaced residents are in inadequate temporary shelter (e.g. ~100 women and children sharing one bathroom at a Bidur shelter; one 250-household community swept away entirely). This is a materially firmer, better-dated version of a story the 2026-09-01 scan carried only as unattributed cross-country context in sector_alerts ('did not attribute the death toll cleanly to a single dated, sourceable incident per country'); this cycle resolves that gap with country-specific, dated, multiply-sourced reporting for Nepal.

entity_reviews.name: Democratic Republic of C
entity_reviews.summary: WHO declared the end of the DRC's 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) epidemic on 2026-08-25 after 42 days without a new confirmed case; a 2026-09-02 case-count update put the final cumulative toll at 6,250 confirmed cases and 3,039 deaths, making it the largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country (PHEIC declared 2026-05-17; expanded to 54 health zones across six provinces). Distinct from the eastern-DRC conflict evidence (dated 2026-08-21) that this entity was already assessed against on 2026-09-01 (last_assessed=2026-09-01 per rotation-state) -- this is new information about the health-system/outbreak-response track, not a reproduction of the prior assessment's evidence.

entity_reviews.name: Boeing
entity_reviews.summary: The FAA disclosed to Reuters on 2026-09-02 (previously undisclosed to the public) that Boeing paid the full $3,139,319 civil penalty proposed in September 2025 for a series of safety violations tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 mid-air door-plug emergency, including presenting two aircraft for certification that were not airworthy and interfering with the independence of company safety officials. Boeing quietly paid the fine in January 2026. The underlying conduct is not new (already within the benchmark's historical record), but the public disclosure -- and its five-plus-month delay -- is new and relevant to transparency/governance scoring; last_assessed 2026-06-10 predates this disclosure.
